research.topic: The first FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay, 13–30 July 1930, entirely in Montevideo, with 13 teams. Uruguay was chosen as reigning Olympic champions (1924, 1928) and for the centenary of its first constitution; the Estadio Centenario, built for the tournament, was completed five days after the opening matches. Only four European teams travelled: France, Belgium and Romania sailed on the SS Conte Verde (picking up Brazil's squad in Rio de Janeiro), Yugoslavia on another ship. Uruguay beat Argentina 4–2 in the final on 30 July 1930. Italy hosted and won the second edition in 1934; Brazil has the most titles (five).
